item.title: Eni, BP aim for final investment decision on Egypt's gas discovery in few months
item.description: Eni is working with BP and Egyptian Petroleum Corporation (EGPC) to reach a final investment decision in the next few months regarding Egypt's recent-discovered gas field Denise West, the Italian energy group said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Eni (ENI.MI) is working with BP (BP.L) and Egyptian Petroleum Corporation (EGPC) to reach a final investment decision in the next few months regarding Egypt's recent-discovered gas field [USN:L8N40Q0IV TEXT:"Denise West"], the Italian energy group said on Tuesday. First gas from the offshore gas discovery, which was announced last April, could come in less than two years, Eni said in a statement. Eni's Chief Executive Claudio Descalzi met Egypt's President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi in Cairo on Tuesday. The country's Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly and the Minister of Petroleum and Mineral Resources Karim Badawi also attended the meeting. Descalzi and El-Sisi also discussed the status of Eni's [USN:L6N43U0JG TEXT:"Cronos gas development"] project in Cyprus' offshore. Cronos will play a crucial role in developing Egypt's status as a Mediterranean energy hub, Eni said. The gas extracted in the Cronos development will be liquefied in Egypt's Damietta LNG plant.

item.title: Greenhushing is killing us: why companies must break their silence on climate change
item.description: Will 2026 be the year we look back at and say “that was the year the climate emergency really started”? We have certainly had many crises over the past few years as global temperatures have risen. But the protracted weather extremes experienced globally, in Europe, North America, and across Asia, make this year feel different.
item.dc:creator: Helen Clarkson
item.content:encoded: Will 2026 be the year we look back at and say “that was the year the climate emergency really started”? We have certainly had many crises over the past few years as global temperatures have risen. But the protracted weather extremes experienced globally, in Europe, North America, and across Asia, make this year feel different. What future historians will puzzle over is why contemporaneous records will show that public discussion of climate change as the root cause didn’t increase. At least in the UK, where I live, the silence got worse. Between 2021 and 2025, climate coverage in media decreased by 38% . In June this year, the UK recorded its then-hottest month on record , but more than 70% of the coverage didn't mention climate change at all. The net-zero policies designed to address the challenge were hardly mentioned, except by outlets frantically peddling misinformation. And while even vehemently anti-climate outlets have recently acknowledged climate change is real (“but we’ve lost, so let’s enjoy the heat”), many news reports about heat and wildfires don’t discuss the root cause. What’s driving this collective silence? First of all, there’s a popular misconception that people don’t like to hear about climate. Yes, people switch off when they hear jargon like “planetary boundaries” or “the clean energy transition”. But research from the Potential Energy Coalition shows climate matters to people when it connects to what they care about: the health of their children, the insurance on their home, the price of their food. Britain's leader of the Conservatives, Kemi Badenoch, has called the 2050 net zero target “impossible” and vowed to repeal the Climate Change Act. REUTERS/Chris J Ratcliffe We see the same appetite around Climate Week NYC, which Climate Group organises every September – we see in our data that registrations and events are much higher than the same time last year. People want to meet and they want to do something about a world that is on fire. Another clear reason for the silence is that climate has once again become extremely politicised. For the last few decades, climate has been a highly political issue in the U.S. And that was even before President Trump, with his support of oil and gas, loathing of wind turbines and banning of the word climate in federal documents. The UK had escaped this politicisation, passing the Climate Change Act in 2008 with cross-party support. The next Conservative prime ministers, up to Boris Johnson, were supportive of green policies, particularly those backed by UK business (for example supporting electric vehicle mandates). But populism and algorithms have let anti-science rhetoric flourish. The UK is now kicking around in the backwash of politicised anti-climate action sentiment from the U.S., fuelling (and fuelled by) disinformation in right-wing media. The most sustained attack is that climate action costs too much and asks too much of ordinary families. In the UK, Reform wants to scrap net zero and axe the government department responsible for it, while the Conservatives’ leader, Kemi Badenoch, has called the 2050 target “impossible” and vowed to repeal the Climate Change Act. Workers on the production line of eDrives used in a variety of Ford electric vehicles, at the Ford Halewood transmissions plant in Liverpool. Britain's clean energy economy generates around 105 billion pounds a year in gross value added. REUTERS/Temilade Adelaja The economics tell a different story. This summer’s heatwaves are set to cost the EU 180 billion euros , and these costs are going to mount, with 2027 forecast to be even worse, due to the building El Niño. In contrast the solution to climate change, net zero, is making the UK money: it’s clean energy economy generates around 105 billion pounds a year in gross value added, supports over 1 million jobs, and has attracted more than 100 billion pounds in private investment since 2024. But you probably won’t have read that in the media or on your social feed. Silence comes at a cost. It breeds inaction, which will slow us down further and cause more pain and suffering. People who care deeply about the climate start to think they’re alone in caring, which saps the momentum for action. Silence is space someone else will fill – usually with climate denial, distraction and disinformation. We can’t afford to cede that ground. Businesses staying silent also matters. It’s dubbed “greenhushing”: companies keeping quiet on their climate goals, wary of political backlash or public scrutiny if they fall short of their targets. Many will say “it’s fine, we can carry on with the same action, we just don’t talk about it”. But that’s only true up to a point. Without the climate urgency, programmes become just another potential choice alongside others that may have a better immediate ROI. We know that people want climate action, they see what’s happening. And collective action problems need collective solutions. What we need is loud voices returning to companies and to the media. And we need some more bravery to stand up for our shared futures.

item.title: Jefe de servicios de inteligencia EEUU visita Rusia para mantener reuniones: medios
item.description: El director de la CIA de Estados Unidos, John Ratcliffe, viajó a Rusia para asistir a unas reuniones en Moscú el martes, según informaron varios medios de comunicación estadounidenses citando fuentes anónimas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El director de la CIA de Estados Unidos, John Ratcliffe, viajó a Rusia para asistir a unas reuniones en Moscú el martes, según informaron varios medios de comunicación estadounidenses citando fuentes anónimas. Tanto CBS News como Axios informaron de la visita del antiguo director de Inteligencia Nacional del presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, que ahora dirige la agencia de espionaje del país. Los medios no precisaron con quién se reunió Ratcliffe ni qué temas se esperaba que se trataran en las conversaciones. Los portavoces de la CIA no respondieron de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios sobre estas informaciones, mientras que no fue posible contactar de inmediato con los portavoces del Kremlin.

item.title: Google expande plataforma de IA para escritórios de advocacia e advogados
item.description: O Google ampliou nesta terça-feira sua plataforma de inteligência artificial Gemini Enterprise com novas ferramentas para advogados e escritórios de advocacia, acelerando a corrida entre as empresas de tecnologia para atender à demanda do setor jurídico por IA.
item.dc:creator: Mike Scarcella
item.content:encoded: O Google (GOOGL.O) ampliou nesta terça-feira sua plataforma de inteligência artificial Gemini Enterprise com novas ferramentas para advogados e escritórios de advocacia, acelerando a corrida entre as empresas de tecnologia para atender à demanda do setor jurídico por IA. A empresa afirmou que o Gemini Enterprise for Legal ajudará escritórios de advocacia a utilizar IA para gerenciar tarefas rotineiras e complexas, permitindo que os advogados se concentrem em serviços de maior valor agregado, ao mesmo tempo em que mantêm seus dados seguros e confidenciais. O novo plug-in para o Gemini Enterprise inclui integração com softwares jurídicos e plataformas de dados, além de um conjunto de agentes de IA que, segundo o Google, podem lidar com funções jurídicas e administrativas especializadas sem supervisão humana significativa. A Alphabet lançou o Gemini Enterprise para clientes empresariais em outubro, em uma tentativa de atrair mais usuários corporativos. O Google Cloud se tornou um dos negócios de crescimento mais rápido da Alphabet. Além da área jurídica, o Google anunciou nesta terça-feira o lançamento de ferramentas para o setor de serviços financeiros. Empresas rivais de IA, incluindo a Anthropic, também expandiram suas ofertas corporativas nos últimos meses, inclusive no setor jurídico. Um relatório de 2026 da Deloitte sobre a adoção de IA pelo setor jurídico constatou que os escritórios de advocacia estão investindo pesadamente na tecnologia como parte de uma transformação que ainda está em seus estágios iniciais. A Thomson Reuters, proprietária da Reuters e do banco de dados de pesquisa jurídica da Westlaw, está entre as concorrentes pela participação no mercado do setor jurídico. Na segunda-feira, ela lançou um modelo de linguagem de grande porte proprietário chamado Thomson 1.0, treinado com seu conteúdo de pesquisa jurídica e desenvolvido para o trabalho profissional. A empresa afirmou que o modelo é baseado em tecnologia de código aberto e se baseia em décadas de seu próprio conteúdo jurídico “oficial”. O Google afirmou que sua plataforma se conectará de forma direta e segura a outras plataformas de tecnologia jurídica pertencentes à Thomson Reuters, à desenvolvedora de software de IA jurídica Harvey, à empresa de análise de dados e tecnologia LexisNexis e a outras. Os escritórios de advocacia estão adotando rapidamente ferramentas de IA generativa que podem auxiliar na pesquisa jurídica, na elaboração de documentos e na execução de outras tarefas jurídicas. Muitos também estão utilizando IA para operações comerciais, como gestão de clientes e de processos, buscando reduzir custos e melhorar a eficiência. A nova oferta do Google foi projetada para ser flexível para os escritórios de advocacia, disse Amrita Mehrok, diretora de produtos do Google Cloud na empresa, permitindo que eles escolham entre os modelos de IA incorporados à plataforma. Alguns grandes escritórios de advocacia formaram parcerias estratégicas com provedores de IA e, em alguns casos, estão desenvolvendo suas próprias plataformas de IA. O Google informou que Weil Gotshal, Cleary Gottlieb, Freshfields e Williams & Connolly estão entre um grupo de escritórios que colaboram com a empresa no projeto Gemini Enterprise for Legal. Jonathon Soler, sócio-gerente da Weil Gotshal, disse em uma entrevista que os clientes esperam cada vez mais que seus advogados utilizem IA e aproveitem suas vantagens em termos de eficiência. Jeffrey Karpf, sócio-gerente da Cleary Gottlieb, disse que a colaboração do escritório com o Google permitá que ele “se envolvea.na criação de ferramentas úteis para escritórios de advocacia que implementam IA”.

item.title: BNP Paribas receives Saudi regional headquarters licence
item.description: BNP Paribas has received a regional headquarters licence in Saudi Arabia, Saudi state news agency SPA reported on Tuesday, as France's biggest bank joins other international companies expanding their presence in the kingdom.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: BNP Paribas (BNPP.PA) has received a regional headquarters licence in Saudi Arabia, Saudi state news agency SPA reported on Tuesday, as France's biggest bank joins other international companies expanding their presence in the kingdom. Saudi Arabia has pushed multinational companies to relocate their regional headquarters to Riyadh in recent years as part of efforts to position the capital as a leading financial hub in the Gulf along with Dubai and Abu Dhabi in neighbouring United Arab Emirates (UAE). The government has said companies without a Riyadh headquarters risk losing access to state contracts. The licence was announced during a Paris meeting between Saudi Arabia's investment minister, Fahd bin Abduljalil al Saif, and BNP Chairman Jean Lemierre, SPA added. BNP's presence in the Middle East includes offices in Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, Kuwait and Bahrain.

item.title: La confianza de los consumidores estadounidenses cae en agosto: The Conference Board
item.description: La confianza de los consumidores estadounidenses cayó en agosto a su nivel más bajo en siete meses, debido al empeoramiento de las perspectivas de los hogares respecto al mercado laboral y la inflación, según reveló una encuesta publicada el martes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La confianza de los consumidores estadounidenses cayó en agosto a su nivel más bajo en siete meses, debido al empeoramiento de las perspectivas de los hogares respecto al mercado laboral y la inflación, según reveló una encuesta publicada el martes. The Conference Board indicó que su índice de confianza de los consumidores descendió este mes a 89,4 unidades -su mínimo desde enero- desde un 90,2 revisado a la baja en julio. Los economistas sondeados por Reuters habían pronosticado una cifra de 90,2, frente al 90,8 comunicado inicialmente en julio. El descenso se debió sobre todo a una caída del 7,8% en el índice de expectativas, lo que contrarrestó la primera mejora en cuatro meses en la percepción de los hogares sobre la situación actual. "Los consumidores se mostraron más pesimistas respecto a la situación empresarial y al mercado laboral de cara a los próximos seis meses", afirmó Dana Peterson, economista jefe de The Conference Board. El denominado índice diferencial de empleo del informe, que mide la diferencia entre los encuestados que afirman que hay muchos puestos de trabajo y los que consideran que es difícil encontrarlos, subió por primera vez en tres meses desde el dato de julio, que fue el más bajo en más de cinco años. Los consumidores prevén que la inflación se acelere al 5,8% en los próximos 12 meses, frente al 5,6 % registrado en julio.

item.title: Ukraine needs changes to avoid losing war, ousted defence minister says
item.description: Ukraine appears to be slowly losing the war against Russia, ousted Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov told Reuters, warning that Kyiv has a window of several months to make key decisions needed to turn the tide in its favour.
item.dc:creator: Max Hunder
item.content:encoded: Ukraine appears to be slowly losing the war against Russia, ousted Defence Minister [USN:L6N44G0JB TEXT:"Mykhailo Fedorov"] told Reuters, warning that Kyiv has a window of several months to make key decisions needed to turn the tide in its favour. Fedorov, a young reformer whose dismissal last month sparked [USN:L8N44H0Q1 TEXT:"weeks of protests"], said Ukraine lacked any overall vision for how to win the four-year-old conflict , and was hobbled by its failure to innovate. Engrained corruption and patronage networks, as well as a lack of political independence in government institutions were also holding the country back, he said in an interview. "I think that there's now a turning point which will determine our future trajectory, but it looks as though we're gradually, slowly losing," Fedorov said in a marked departure from Kyiv's official rhetoric. Ukraine still had "every chance" to win but urgently needed a plan to end the war, he added. Ukraine’s presidential office said in response to Fedorov’s comments that he had been positive about the conduct of the war when he was at the ministry and the only thing that had changed was his personal status. LACK OF INTERCEPTORS HINDERS UKRAINE Russia is hammering Ukrainian factories and warehouses with [USN:L1N44H0GB TEXT:"dozens of ballistic missiles"] a month, which Ukraine is mostly unable to take down as interceptors run low. Although Russia is gaining less ground than last year, it is still slowly crawling forward in the Donbas, while Ukraine's sparse frontline infantry dugouts are manned mostly by unmotivated conscripts. Ukraine, in turn, has ramped up its own drone and missile attacks [USN:L8N41Q0NS TEXT:"deep into Russia"], hitting some key military factories, causing serious damage to [USN:L1N44L0IX TEXT:"oil refineries"] and creating nationwide fuel shortages. A poll conducted at the end of July found 82% of Ukrainians believed Ukraine would win, although most expected fighting to carry on into 2027 or later. Fedorov, 35, was fired six months after his appointment, having initiated reforms around procurement and mobilisation that put him on a collision course with the military establishment and political rivals. Last week, he rocked Ukrainian politics by becoming the first major political figure to demand wartime elections, decrying a "systemic" crisis of governance. In an interview on Monday, he emphasised the importance of developing autonomous drones guided by artificial intelligence, cheap interceptor missiles to stop Russia's air attacks and Ukraine's own ballistic missile program to turn the tide of the war. Ukrainian manufacturers are already working on those technologies, but Fedorov said the country needed a joined-up strategy to maximise their effect once deployed. He laid out a vision for a frontline covered by electronic sensors to detect enemies, with drones on land and in the air to minimise human presence. "Technologies exist already which could completely stop the Russians, but our absence of vision ... means we do not apply them," he said. Fedorov criticised the wasted potential and inefficiency of the Ukrainian state, which he said was operating at "5% effectiveness." BUDGET DEFICIT BLAME GAME Fedorov says he was a driving force behind a drone campaign this year targeting Russia's fuel and military logistics in the occupied part of southern Ukraine, causing problems for Moscow's forces on the frontline. He said there was still a window of opportunity of a few months to press ahead with that operation, seeking to isolate Russian-occupied Crimea, before Russia works out how to respond to Ukraine's tactics. [USN:L8N41Q0NS TEXT:"This strike campaign"] was a significant factor in shifting narratives about Ukraine's prospects. Fedorov previously said the campaign's success was aided by his decision to front-load spending, which had been earmarked for the second half of 2026. President Volodymyr Zelenskiy — Fedorov's former political patron turned rival — said at the weekend that bringing spending forward had left a $27 billion hole in the ministry's budget, for which donor-dependent Ukraine does not have a solution. Fedorov said he had no idea where Zelenskiy got this figure, arguing his ministry devised a spending plan that relied on savings from new procurement tenders and international support. Fedorov alleged that when he arrived at the defence ministry, he found department heads appointed at the behest of Ukrainian defence companies to lobby for their interests. "By the end of the year, the budget deficit under our planning was around five billion dollars, and we knew where we would get it," he said. "Perhaps the plan changed and new projects emerged that require such a budget." ELECTION CALL Fedorov's call for elections was [USN:L8N44H0Q1 TEXT:"met with dismay from many Ukrainians"] and polls have consistently shown low enthusiasm for wartime elections. Zelenskiy condemned Fedorov's election call, arguing it could destroy Ukraine as it fights off Russia. Ukraine has, since Russia's February 2022 invasion, been under martial law which bans elections for security reasons. The president said Fedorov may be being pushed by outside forces to call for elections. Fedorov staunchly denied this. While there are [USN:L1N44G089 TEXT:"enormous logistical challenges to holding wartime elections"], Fedorov said that Ukraine would find innovative solutions. However, he said it was too early to say if he would run for the presidency. In the meantime, Fedorov plans to split his time between his push to restore Ukraine's elections and ventures focused on innovative military technologies, including an investment fund for which he plans to raise capital during an upcoming trip to the U.S.

item.title: Iraq may show how U.S. can squeeze Iran's trade partners
item.description: Iraq could serve as an example of how the United States could carry out its threat to force countries that continue trading with Iran out of the dollar-based financial system.
item.dc:creator: Michael Georgy
item.content:encoded: Iraq could serve as an example of how the [USN:L6N44M07H TEXT:"United States could carry out its threat"] to force [USN:L6N44H0PZ TEXT:"countries that continue trading with Iran"] out of the dollar-based financial system. Washington has already [USN:L5N3P706O TEXT:"sanctioned a host of Iraqi banks"] accused of doing business with Tehran, though it has avoided measures that would devastate the economy of the strategic ally of both countries. U.S. President Donald Trump has warned that any country that provides Iran with an economic lifeline would face severe consequences. That could put [USN:L6N44H0PZ TEXT:"Iran's main trading partners"] of recent years in the frame: China, the United Arab Emirates, Turkey, India, Pakistan and Oman. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday announced "[USN:L6N44M0FC TEXT:"an economic onslaught"]" against Iran with sanctions, saying its trading partners would be targeted, without naming them. HOW THE U.S. INFLUENCES THE IRAQI ECONOMY The United States, since its 2003 invasion of Iraq, has held effective control over [USN:L6N3YM0P3 TEXT:"the country's oil revenue dollars"], primarily through the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, giving Washington extraordinary leverage over Baghdad's affairs. A rare ally of both the United States and Iran, with more than $100 billion in reserves held in the U.S., Iraq relies heavily on Washington's goodwill to keep its oil revenues and finances flowing. Reuters revealed in late 2024 a [USN:L1N3LQ0HI TEXT:"fuel oil smuggling network"] generating at least $1 billion a year for Iran and its proxies in Iraq. Other neighbours of Iran involved in similar schemes could face similar scrutiny from Washington. While the U.S. has uniquely strong leverage over Iraq compared with other major trading partners of Iran, the U.S. dollar's status as the linchpin of global trade makes its reach formidable. WHAT MEASURES HAS THE U.S. ALREADY TAKEN AGAINST IRAQ? In April, Reuters reported the U.S. [USN:P8N3T708B TEXT:"halted a $500 million cash "][USN:P8N3T708B TEXT:"shipment"] to Iraq and suspended parts of security cooperation to pressure Baghdad over Iran-backed militias. In January, Washington reportedly threatened senior Iraqi politicians with sanctions — including on oil revenues — should such groups join the next government. Successive U.S. administrations have sought to choke that dollar stream with sanctions on Iraqi banks in recent years, though some of the largest banks were spared. Iraq's current prime minister emerged as a candidate seen as acceptable to the Trump administration, which has steadily pressured Baghdad to curb Tehran's influence. U.S. pressure has raised the costs and risks of financial dealings with Iran, forcing Iraqi institutions to improve compliance, said Neil Quilliam, associate fellow at UK-based think tank Chatham House. But it hasn't broken Iraq's economic ties with Iran, which extend beyond the financial system — leaving Baghdad caught between its dependence on both Washington and Tehran. "Countries such as China or Turkey have larger economies and more room to absorb pressure. Iraq has fewer alternatives and significantly less financial resilience," Quilliam said. "Its vulnerability comes less from the scale of its trade with Iran and more from its dependence on continued access to the U.S.-led financial architecture." WHAT ARE IRAQ'S TRADE TIES WITH IRAN? Iraq's trade with Iran topped $10 billion in 2025, according to official figures, driven mainly by Iranian exports of food and consumer goods to the Iraqi market. Trade has fallen in 2026 after the Iran war began, raising security risks, disrupting border crossings and increasing transport costs. Iran has long viewed its neighbour and ally Iraq as an economic "lung" and wields considerable military, political and economic influence there through the powerful Shi'ite militias and political parties it backs. It has also sourced hard currency from Iraq through exports and has avoided U.S. sanctions via its neighbour's banking system. Energy is central to the relationship: Iraq pays Iran $4 billion to $5 billion a year for natural gas used to generate electricity, Iraqi energy officials say, and officials warn new U.S. measures could jeopardise those payments. WILL ANY NEW U.S. MEASURES AGAINST IRAQ BE EFFECTIVE? Iraq has long been an effective sanctions-evasion route for Iran, said Tom Keatinge, director at the Centre for Finance and Security at the Royal United Services Institute. "As Iran's connections with the international financial system are squeezed further, existing vulnerabilities will find themselves exploited to a greater extent. In that regard, Iraq, its banking system and its informal financial sector can expect to face mounting challenges," he added. He said, however, that an approach based on incentives rather than punitive measures could be more effective. For example, the U.S. could provide technical assistance for the Iraqi central bank and the broader Iraqi government in "a strategy based on carrots rather than sticks," he added. The U.S. is also wary of wider fallout for the financial system. Asked why he stopped short of penalising Iran directly or naming targeted countries, Bessent said: "Why would I want to blow up the global financial system?"

item.title: Monedas cotizan sin grandes cambios en línea con movimientos del dólar; analizan sanciones a Irán
item.description: Las principales monedas de América Latina cotizaban con un sesgo bajista aunque sin grandes movimientos el martes, en línea con la estabilidad del dólar, mientras los inversores seguían analizando las sanciones impuestas a Irán y a la espera de datos clave para los futuros movimientos de las tasas de interés.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Farías
item.content:encoded: Las principales monedas de América Latina cotizaban con un sesgo bajista aunque sin grandes movimientos el martes, en línea con la estabilidad del dólar, mientras los inversores seguían analizando las sanciones impuestas a Irán y a la espera de datos clave para los futuros movimientos de las tasas de interés. * El dólar operaba estable el martes, aunque seguía expuesto al riesgo de nuevas caídas mientras los inversores analizan las sanciones ampliadas de Washington contra Irán y los nuevos esfuerzos por aliviar la presión sobre el rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro a más largo plazo. * En los mercados también había atención a los esfuerzos del Tesoro por apuntalar los precios de los bonos a largo plazo y hacer caer los retornos, para así aliviar los costos de endeudamiento. El secretario del Tesoro de Estados Unidos, Scott Bessent, inquietó a los inversores la semana pasada al anunciar que se duplicaría el volumen de las recompras trimestrales de bonos a más largo plazo. * En el mercado de deuda, el rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro a más largo plazo caía el martes al tocar los precios del crudo un mínimo de una semana, mientras los operadores siguen sopesando las implicaciones de la decisión de Bessent de ampliar las recompras de bonos. * Mientras, Irán prometió responder a la ampliación de las sanciones estadounidenses destinadas a aislar su economía, expresó su confianza en que sus principales socios comerciales resistirían la campaña de presión y afirmó que Washington estaba interesado en reactivar las conversaciones. * Además, la presidenta de la Fed de Boston, Susan Collins, dijo que el banco central necesitará subir las tasas de interés pronto a menos de que los próximos datos muestren un continuo declive en la inflación. * El peso mexicano subía un 0,04%, a 16,9356 unidades por dólar y se mantenía por debajo de la barrera de 17 unidades por dólar; en tanto que el índice S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) , integrado por las 35 acciones más líquidas del mercado, bajaba un 0,33%, a 65.555,42 puntos, después de cuatro sesiones de alzas. * "La moneda local muestra un comportamiento lateral con sesgo a la baja, impulsado por la tendencia del dólar y una moderada recuperación del apetito por riesgo entre los inversores", dijo la correduría Monex, que estimó un nivel de soporte en 16,90 por dólar y uno de resistencia en 17,00 unidades. * El real brasileño ganaba un 0,16% a 5,1444 por dólar, al tiempo que el referencial bursátil Bovespa (.BVSP) descendía un 0,15% a 171.642 puntos. * El peso colombiano se depreciaba un 0,58% a 3.074,85 unidades por dólar, en su segunda sesión de pérdidas; al tiempo que el índice accionario de la bolsa, el MSCI COLCAP (.COLCAP) retrocedía un 0,36% a 2.501,63 puntos. * El peso chileno , se apreciaba un 0,34%, a 909,40/909,70 unidades por dólar, en medio de la estabilidad de la divisa estadounidense en los mercados globales. Por su parte, el principal índice de la bolsa de comercio de Santiago, el IPSA (.SPIPSA) retrocedía un 1,41%, a 11.374,73 puntos. * El peso mayorista argentino se depreciaba un leve 0,07% a 1.511 por dólar, luego de abrir en su récord mínimo interbancario de 1.512 unidades. El peso seguía presionado por coberturas en dólares que le hacían renovar su piso histórico a un día de que se fije el tipo de cambio para un millonario vencimiento de deuda doméstica. * La moneda peruana, el sol , se apreciaba un mínimo 0,03% a 3,3440/3,3460 unidades por dólar, mientras que la Bolsa de Lima (.MXNUAMPESCPGPE) perdía un 0,21% a 1.570,23 puntos.

item.title: Guinea-Bissau to vote on new constitution that would expand presidential powers
item.description: Guinea-Bissau, which is currently led by military officers who staged a coup last year, will hold a constitutional referendum on August 30 that would expand the power of the presidency and reshape rules for elections scheduled for December.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Guinea-Bissau, which is currently led by military officers who staged a coup last year, will hold a constitutional referendum on August 30 that would expand the power of the presidency and reshape rules for elections scheduled for December. Under the current constitution, Guinea-Bissau's legislature names a prime minister who appoints a cabinet. The new constitution would allow the president to appoint and dismiss the prime minister and cabinet. The president would also be able to create or abolish government ministries, chair the Council of Ministers, dissolve parliament in the event of a grave political crisis and dismiss the government under certain circumstances, according to a copy seen by Reuters. The new constitution would also shrink parliament to 65 seats from 102 and cut the number of electoral constituencies to 12 from 29. The [USN:L8N3X80SH TEXT:"coup last November"] took place one day before the electoral commission was due to announce the results of a presidential election. The reduction in electoral constituencies could curb the influence of parties with strong local bases said Manuel said Nobre de Barros, a professor at Lusofona University in Guinea Bissau. More broadly, the reforms would alter the balance of power between the president and the legislature, de Barros said. "The changes give the president absolute power under the new constitution, with no political opposition," he said. The constitution would require presidential candidates to have resided permanently in Guinea-Bissau for the previous five years, a condition not included in the current constitution, which requires candidates to be Guinean citizens by birth, at least 35 years old and in full possession of civil and political rights.

item.title: Video muestra daños causados por el terremoto de Venezuela, no de Colombia
item.description: Un video que muestra a un grupo de búsqueda entre los escombros de edificios en Venezuela tras los terremotos a finales de junio fue erróneamente relacionado con el sismo del 10 de agosto en Colombia.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Un video que muestra a un grupo de búsqueda entre los escombros de edificios en Venezuela tras los terremotos a finales de junio fue erróneamente relacionado con el sismo del 10 de agosto en Colombia. Estos son los detalles clave: Publicaciones en Facebook describen el video como la búsqueda en Colombia de personas entre escombros de construcciones. El 10 de agosto un [USN:L1N3AC29B TEXT:"terremoto"] de magnitud 7.4 golpeó el oeste del país que dejó, al 24 de agosto, 494 personas muertas. Reuters geolocalizó el video en la ciudad costera de La Guaira, cerca de la capital Caracas. Algunos edificios coinciden con imágenes satelitales de Google Earth. Dos [USN:S0N3LX0EG TEXT:"terremotos"] de magnitud 7.2 y 7.5 el 24 de junio causaron daños extensos, incluido el derrumbe de edificios en Venezuela. La compañía Gideon Rescue Company publicó el clip el 2 de julio con una descripción sobre el sismo en Venezuela. Según su sitio web , la empresa se dedica a labores de rescate en zonas de desastre y conflicto. En el segundo 0:24 del video aparece una persona que viste una prenda con las iniciales de la compañía junto a un bombero de Caracas. La compañía dijo a Reuters en un mensaje de WhatsApp el 13 de agosto que un miembro de su equipo grabó el video tras los terremotos en Venezuela y compartió imágenes de su equipo en las operaciones de rescate. Algunos elementos del clip compartido en línea coinciden con los de videos de Reuters grabados el 28 y 29 de junio en La Guaira . El 24 de agosto, Jorge Rodríguez, presidente de la Asamblea Nacional de Venezuela, dijo en sus redes sociales que los sismos en el país mataron a 6,509 personas. Veredicto: Erróneamente etiquetado. El video muestra escombros de edificios derrumbados en La Guaira, Venezuela, tras los terremotos del 25 junio. Reuters Fact Check ofrece información confiable mediante su canal de WhatsApp para México . Envíenos un mensaje con el contenido en español que desea que verifiquemos. Este artículo fue realizado por el equipo de Reuters Fact Check. Lea más sobre nuestro trabajo de verificación de afirmaciones en las redes sociales.

item.title: US rates need to rise soon absent evidence of ongoing drop in inflation, Fed's Collins says
item.description: The U.S. Federal Reserve will need to raise interest rates soon unless coming data show a continued decline in inflation that remains too high and which has become a "pervasive" concern for businesses and households, Boston Fed President Susan Collins said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Howard Schneider
item.content:encoded: The U.S. Federal Reserve will need to raise interest rates soon unless coming data show a continued decline in inflation that remains too high and which has become a "pervasive" concern for businesses and households, Boston Fed President Susan Collins said on Tuesday. Collins said in comments posted to the Boston Fed website that the current Fed policy rate, under her base case outlook, will continue to push down prices and help with a "gradual disinflation" aided also by the recent rise in longer-term bond yields and other factors. But "should evidence of sustained inflation progress not materialize, I believe it will be appropriate to tighten policy soon to ensure we deliver price stability in a reasonable time frame. ... Concerns about high prices are pervasive in my conversations with stakeholders across New England," Collins wrote. Economists polled by Reuters expect that new inflation data on Wednesday will show that the Personal Consumption Expenditures price index, excluding food and energy, increased at a 3.3% annual rate in July, unchanged from the month before and well above the Fed's 2% target. Core PCE, considered a guide to future headline inflation, has risen steadily since last year, with Fed officials citing the Trump administration's import tariffs , higher oil prices due to the war with Iran, and now massive investments in artificial intelligence as reasons for the increase. The Fed's policy rate, currently in the 3.5% to 3.75% range, has been on hold since December as officials waited for inflation to ease. Collins said she still thinks that may happen, but, with inflation above target for more than five years now, she also said the Fed cannot wait forever, and is concerned that further time missing the inflation goal could shift consumer expectations in a way that makes the inflation goal harder to achieve. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh speaks on Thursday in a much-anticipated keynote address to the central bank's annual research symposium in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, remarks that come amid division on the Fed about the need for rate hikes, and a rise in U.S. Treasury yields.

item.title: Canada announces retaliatory tariffs on $20 billion worth of US goods, unveils support measures
item.description: Canada on Tuesday announced retaliatory tariffs on C$27.6 billion ($19.94 billion) worth of United States goods, matching dollar-for-dollar new duties imposed by Washington, and unveiled financial support for Canadian businesses and workers caught in the escalating trade war.
item.dc:creator: Promit Mukherjee
item.content:encoded: Canada on Tuesday announced retaliatory tariffs on C$27.6 billion ($19.94 billion) worth of United States goods, matching dollar-for-dollar new duties imposed by Washington, and unveiled financial support for Canadian businesses and workers caught in the escalating trade war. The counter-tariffs take effect on U.S. goods from September 8 and will impose duties of 15%, 25% and 50% across 700 products imported from south of the border, a government statement said. In terms of financial support for affected workers and industries, Canada announced a C$7.5 billion package of new and enhanced measures including support for small and medium-sized businesses, a stream for funding cash flows of companies, and support for workers who could be at risk due to the new tariffs. From Saturday, President Donald Trump's new 50% tariffs across[USN:T5N43900P TEXT:" $20 billion"] of Canadian imports took effect after talks between the two countries to avert the tariffs collapsed. The new tit-for-tat tariffs mark a new low in the Canada-U.S. relationship. "Our dollar-for-dollar, rate for rate counter-tariffs as well as a multi-billion dollar support package will protect workers, farmers, families, and businesses," Canada's Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne said. The new tariffs are designed so that the impact on Canadian consumers and businesses is minimal and could still hit the U.S., a government official said. The 50% tariffs are on some important sectors such as steel, aluminum, furniture and clothing, 25% tariffs are on cheese, appliances and some seafood, while the 15% tariffs will be on electronics and tools, the official said.

item.title: Rimbalza su ripresa settore tech, attesi risultati Nvidia, dati inflazione
item.description: I principali indici di Wall Street sono in rialzo grazie alla ripresa dei titoli tech dopo un sell-off in attesa dei risultati del colosso IA Nvidia e di una lettura sull'inflazione fondamentale per delineare le aspettative sui tassi di interesse.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: I principali indici di Wall Street sono in rialzo grazie alla ripresa dei titoli tech dopo un sell-off in attesa dei risultati del colosso IA Nvidia e di una lettura sull'inflazione fondamentale per delineare le aspettative sui tassi di interesse. ** I rialzi potrebbero placare i timori degli investitori scatenati dalla recente flessione del mercato obbligazionario, che ha spinto al rialzo i rendimenti e messo sotto pressione l'azionario. Potrebbero inoltre contribuire a definire l’andamento del mercato prima di settembre, mese tendenzialmente debole per l'azionario. ** La sostenibilità di questo rally, alimentato dalle trimestrali, potrebbe però essere messa nuovamente alla prova questa settimana con la pubblicazione dei risultati di Nvidia (NVDA.O) , in agenda per domani. ** La maggior parte delle megacap è in rialzo, con NVIDIA (NVDA.O) e META (META.O) che guadagnano rispettivamente il 2,4% e l'1%. ** Tra i produttori di chip, INTEL (INTC.O) e MICRON (MU.O) ottengono l'1,9% ciascuno. La società di archiviazione dati WESTERN DIGITAL (WDC.O) sale dell'1,2%. ** ADVANCED MICRO DEVICES (AMD.O) registra un rialzo del 3,9% dopo che Raymond James ha rivisto al rialzo il rating del titolo. ** Intorno alle 16.20 l’indice Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) sale dello 0,09% a 53.462,86, l’S&P 500 (.SPX) guadagna lo 0,29% a 7.674,77 e il Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) ottiene lo 0,53% a 26.118,97.

item.title: Trump says Strait of Hormuz has been demined, warns Iran not to plant more
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that all mines had been detonated or removed from international waters of the Strait of Hormuz and that Iran has been told that any ship or boat placing new mines will be destroyed.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that all mines had been detonated or removed from international waters of the Strait of Hormuz and that Iran has been told that any ship or boat placing new mines will be destroyed. In a post on Truth Social, Trump said the United States, through its Space Force, was watching "every square inch" of the Strait, a key waterway in the global energy supply chain. "There is a Zero Tolerance policy on mine placement in full force and effect," Trump said. The U.S. and Iran have not conducted air strikes on each other's militaries for weeks, but attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz have continued as the two sides vie for control of the narrow maritime passage. Oil transits through the strait were at 5 million barrels per day on Monday, provisional data from shiptracker Vortexa showed, down from more than 20 million per day before the war or about one of every five barrels consumed worldwide.

item.title: Report: Big Ten to ban returnees from NFL
item.description: The Big Ten intends to approve a rule change that will ban football players who have been with an NFL team from returning to college football at one of its member schools, ESPN reported Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Big Ten intends to approve a rule change that will ban football players who have been with an NFL team from returning to college football at one of its member schools, ESPN reported Tuesday. The rule is expected to be approved Tuesday and will apply to any player whose name has appeared on an NFL roster or signed a pro contract. The rule also will apply to players who declared for the draft and did not withdraw before the deadline, per the report. The Southeastern Conference has also discussed a ban on players returning from professional football. The league's presidents and chancellors released a statement Monday saying athletes who have signed pro contracts "should not then be permitted" to return to college sports. "College athletes, not former professional athletes, have been at the heart of the Southeastern Conference. Individuals who choose to leave college athletics, sign professional playing contracts, and compete professionally should not then be permitted to return to college competition," the statement read. "Allowing that to occur will blur the line between college and professional sports, create significant competitive equity concerns, and reduce opportunities for high school and current college athletes." For now, LSU head coach Lane Kiffin is taking advantage of a judge's ruling that grants them another year of eligibility. Tight end Dae'Quan Wright, who played for Kiffin at Ole Miss over the past two seasons, reportedly plans to join LSU once he clears NFL waivers. Wright returns from time spent with the Cleveland Browns. On Monday, former Ole Miss defensive lineman Zxavian Harris, who was waived by the New Orleans Saints, revealed on his Instagram account that he also intends to join Kiffin at LSU, labeling it a "business decision." Wright, Harris and 14 other players have only one additional year of NCAA eligibility thanks to a Louisiana court that granted them a temporary restraining order last week, allowing them to enter the transfer portal to keep their options open. The order is related to the NCAA's new age-based eligibility model, which allows five seasons within a five-year window and did not cover players from the high school Class of 2022 who had already exhausted their eligibility. Kiffin defended his decision to add the players on Monday. "At the end of the day, because of these rulings, they're either going to play for you or they're going to play for someone else around the country," Kiffin said. --Field Level Media

item.title: ULTIM'ORA-DAZI: Trump minaccia di cambiare nome Lago Ontario in Lago America in disputa con Canada
item.description: Il presidente Usa Donald Trump ha minacciato di portare i dazi su una serie di prodotti canadesi al 50% dopo il fallimento dei colloqui tra i due Paesi sul commercio venerdì scorso, e Ottawa ha risposto annunciando che farà lo stesso. Di seguito gli aggiornamenti:
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Il presidente Usa Donald Trump ha minacciato di portare i dazi su una serie di prodotti canadesi al 50% dopo il fallimento dei colloqui tra i due Paesi sul commercio venerdì scorso, e Ottawa ha risposto annunciando che farà lo stesso. Di seguito gli aggiornamenti: 16.40 - Il presidente Donald Trump ha detto che sta valutando la possibilità di cambiare il nome del Lago Ontario in Lago America, mentre la guerra commerciale tra Usa e Canada si inasprisce. "Gli Stati Uniti stanno seriamente valutando la possibilità di cambiare il nome del Lago Ontario in Lago America dato che non prevediamo di intrattenere più molti rapporti commerciali con l’Ontario", ha scritto Trump in un post su Truth Social. Interrogato in merito al commento di Trump, il ministro canadese responsabile per il commercio con gli Stati Uniti, Dominic LeBlanc, ha detto che il Canada non risponderà ai post sui social media dell’amministrazione statunitense.

item.title: Honda says it may not build new plant in North America without trade deal extension
item.description: A senior Honda executive said the Japanese automaker might not build an eighth assembly plant in North America unless a key trade deal is extended.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A senior Honda (7267.T) executive said the Japanese automaker might not build an eighth assembly plant in North America unless a key trade deal is extended. Honda Executive Vice President Noriya Kaihara told reporters at a roundtable in Washington the automaker is close to full production capacity in North America and needs a new factory. The Trump administration is currently negotiating with Canada and Mexico over the fate of the free trade deal known as USMCA. "If there is no USMCA agreement in the future, we may have to change our direction," Kaihara said, adding the company will need to make a decision within a year or two and would like the plant to be running by around 2030.

item.title: Too much information, not enough understanding: Opella’s push for health literacy
item.description: Underpinning modern consumer capitalism lies one simple yet profoundly powerful concept: the idea of choice.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Balch
item.content:encoded: Underpinning modern consumer capitalism lies one simple yet profoundly powerful concept: the idea of choice. Presented with two options, Product A and Product B, the edifice of modern consumerism rests on persuading shoppers to select one over the other. But what if consumers become so bombarded with information (and misinformation) that their ability to make good choices becomes compromised? It’s precisely this scenario that Marissa Saretsky, chief sustainability officer at the French consumer healthcare drug company Opella, believes is playing out across consumer markets the world over. “We are living in an unprecedented time where … there's too much information and consumers actually do not know how to understand it,” she states. As the world’s third-largest consumer healthcare company, Opella has a front-row seat to the barrage of advice and information now arising from web and mobile ads, social media platforms, and AI chatbots, in addition to traditional media. The company operates in more than 100 markets worldwide and counts a portfolio of over 100 brands, including household names such as Buscopan (cramp relief), Allegra (antihistamine) and Doliprane (painkiller). Marissa Saretsky, chief sustainability officer at the French consumer healthcare drug company Opella. Handout via REUTERS The effects of information overload on purchasing patterns is stark, says Saretsky, with more and more consumers either buying products that don’t meet their needs or using products in what she describes as the “wrong way”. A third scenario is that consumers end up buying nothing at all. “You may go online and you might find 10 different recommendations, and it's paralysing,” she says. In most consumer sectors, this “information paradox”, as she puts it, manifests primarily as a business-only problem. If a shopper mistakenly buys a silver-plated necklace believing it to be pure silver, for instance, the result is a bad review or returns request. With consumer healthcare, however, the ramifications extend beyond the bottom line. Picture the consumer overdosing on non-prescription painkillers because they got the wrong dosage, or buying a remedy that makes a mild illness worse, rather than better. Such outcomes are not hypothetical, Saretsky says. According to Opella’s research, four in five people lack the confidence to make decisions about their own health. Rather than seek over-the-counter help for mild symptoms, therefore, many turn to their doctor or attend hospital, putting unnecessary pressure on the health system in the process. Saretsky says Opella’s solution is to give consumers what they need to pursue their own self-care. “We want to help people understand what information is the right information for them … and then help guide them into making the right choice,” she explains. Boxes of Doliprane are displayed for sale in a pharmacy in Paris, France, July 16, 2024, when Opella was part of the French pharmaceutical giant Sanofi. REUTERS/Benoit Tessier Opella calls this strategy health literacy , which forms a core part of the “healthy people” pillar of its three-pronged sustainability strategy , alongside “healthy planet” and “healthy business”. The company’s commitment to them extends to a pledge to improve the health literacy of 50 million people annually. Saretsky is anxious to point out that the notion of health literacy isn’t of Opella’s making. Instead, it originates instead with the World Health Organization (WHO), which deploys it as part of its drive to provide universal health coverage worldwide. So, in an already information-saturated marketplace, how does Opella plan to cut through the noise and genuinely empower consumers to make good decisions for their own health? Saretsky’s first response centres on the importance of providing clarity. That starts with the language on or in product packaging, she says: “You shouldn't have to unfold this giant piece of paper. You should be able to pick up a box and very easily find how much to take and how often and for which indications.” The same strategy applies to advertising. Ads should not just promote the benefits of a particular headache pill or anti-cramping tablet, but leave consumers clearer on how and when a product is best used – or, indeed, whether they need to use it at all. Here, Opella looks to integrate the WHO’s four skills of health literacy, namely, the ability to “access”, “understand”, “appraise” and “use” health-related information in a way that promotes consumers’ health. Brands should also look to co-opt trusted third parties in their clarity-making efforts, she advises. Hence, Opella’s recent five-year partnership with the International Pharmaceutical Federation (FIP), the goal of which is to “elevate” the global role of pharmacists in the cause of health literacy. A healthcare worker examines a child at a village on the outskirts of Ahmedabad, India. The World Health Organization defines health literacy as the ability to access, understand, appraise and use health information. REUTERS/Amit Dave The first step of its FIP tie-in focuses on surveying pharmacists about how they help consumers improve their approach to “self-care”. Further down the track, the company plans to use the findings to develop training materials for FIP members. Moves to simplify Opella’s on-pack messaging and in-pack information are similarly in their early days, with trials to introduce e-leaflets marking the frontier of its efforts to date. In the company’s defence, the ink on its sustainability strategy is barely dry. Opella itself only came into being as a stand-alone entity in April 2025, after French pharmaceutical giant Sanofi sold its controlling stake in the firm to private equity. Looking ahead, high levels of regulation in the sector are a barrier, Saretsky admits, as are the different ways that consumers access healthcare in different markets. “In one country, we're seeing it might be the aunt or uncle; in another country, it might be the pharmacist; and, in other countries, digital platforms might be the key place that people go to.” But how does the company account for the possibility that increased consumer education will result in a drop in sales? Take multivitamins, for instance. According to the UK National Health Service, most people can get “all the nutrients they need” by eating a varied and balanced diet. Give consumers good dietary advice, and millions might reasonably stop buying vitamin supplements . The same logic could apply to the supermarket that educates shoppers about the food miles of exotic imported fruits, for example, or to the clothing retailer that advertises the limited number of washes an item can realistically endure. Saretsky argues that it’s far more important for companies to play the long game and secure lasting consumer trust. “Because they trust us, the next time they need something, they'll say, ‘That's a company that I believe.’” Securing consumer trust is also one of the reasons Opella pursued certification as a B Corp, which it achieved in April 2025, the first global consumer healthcare company to do so. Yet Saretsky maintains that the true yardstick is not a label or certificate. As its new sustainability strategy holds, success for Opella will come from equipping consumers to make the best possible health choices, for themselves and the wider world.

item.title: US tariff threat upends copper surplus as prices test all-time peak
item.description: The prospect of U.S. import tariffs could push copper prices to record highs even though there is no global shortage of the metal, analysts say, as the incentive to ship to the United States drains inventories elsewhere.
item.dc:creator: Tom Daly
item.content:encoded: The prospect of U.S. import tariffs could push copper prices to record highs even though there is no global shortage of the metal, analysts say, as the incentive to ship to the United States drains inventories elsewhere. Three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange rose to as high as $14,343 per metric ton on Tuesday, within striking distance of the $14,527.50 record, after [USN:L1N44L08X TEXT:"orders to withdraw"] 65,400 tons of metal from LME warehouses in recent days. The large-scale orders - known as warrant cancellations - came after last week's increase in available material on the LME and the [USN:AZN4TFN24 TEXT:"Shanghai Futures Exchange"] appeared to ease concerns about tight supplies. Analysts said the rally reflects a shortage of copper available outside the U.S. rather than a global deficit of the metal, which is critical for power grids, electric vehicles and AI datacentres. Higher U.S. prices have encouraged traders to ship metal into COMEX warehouses ahead of a potential tariff on refined copper from 2027, running down inventories elsewhere and leaving what was expected to be a surplus market looking far tighter in practice. TARIFF THREAT RESHAPES MARKET The threat of tariffs has turned what should have been a surplus this year into "at best a balanced market", assuming copper stockpiled in the U.S. is no longer available, said Robert Edwards, principal copper analyst at CRU. COMEX inventories have now risen for 46 straight days to a record 675,185 metric tons through an arbitrage trade that capitalises on higher COMEX prices. CRU last projected a 639,000 ton global copper surplus for 2026. "If (U.S.) imports keep coming in as they have been, then it's going to look like a deficit market in reality," Edwards said. The U.S. imported almost 885,000 tons of refined copper cathodes in the first half of 2026, some 3% more than in the same period last year, when a similar tariff threat hung over the market, and more than double imports in the first six months of 2024. The U.S. imported a record 1.64 million tons in the full year of 2025. Refined copper was ultimately given an exemption from the tariffs last year, which initially sent prices plummeting. But the U.S. Commerce Department was due to report to the White House on copper markets by June 30 this year, so that President Donald Trump could decide whether to go ahead with a 15% tariff from January 1, 2027, rising to 30% from 2028. "Based on our numbers, you're looking at years for that metal to get consumed," said Macquarie strategist Alice Fox, referring to COMEX copper stocks. While Macquarie sees greater downside risks for copper, prices would "massively spike" if Trump proceeds with a tariff, she added. GLENCORE SAYS UNCERTAINTY, NOT TARIFFS, IS DRIVING RALLY The CEO of miner and trader Glencore (GLEN.L) , however, believes any announcement on tariffs - whether imposing a zero, 15% or 30% duty - is likely to see prices fall because the market will finally have better clarity on the situation. "You'll have these high stockpiles in the U.S., which over time will be drawn down for use ... not to be exported again" due to the costs involved, Gary Nagle said on an earnings call. Copper stored in COMEX warehouses is already duty-paid. If those inventories stay in the United States, other regions would continue to face tighter supplies. China, the world's largest copper-smelting nation, has limited capacity to offset shortages elsewhere because of strong domestic demand, according to Amelia Fu, head of commodities market strategy at Bank of China International. Low stocks, mine disruption and an outage at the [USN:L1N449013 TEXT:"Gresik smelter"] in Indonesia are tightening the market, Fu said. "We could see new record highs in copper prices in coming weeks or months."

item.title: Wildberger: Sollten als Zwischenziel Platz 3 im KI-Rennen anstreben
item.description: Digitalminister Karsten Wildberger hat mit Blick auf die nötige Aufholjagd bei Künstlicher Intelligenz vor falschen Zielen gewarnt. "Es geht nicht immer nur darum, die Nummer eins zu sein", sagte Wildberger am Dienstag am Rande der Kabinettsklausur in Neuhardenberg. Deutschland sei die drittgrößte Volkswirtschaft, "und ich würde mal sagen, das Ziel, Nummer drei, Nummer vier zu sein in der Welt, ist auch mal ein gutes Zwischenziel", fügte er hinzu. Zwar seien Amerikaner und Chinesen beim Thema KI tatsächlich enteilt. Aber zum einen habe auch China mit weniger Ressourcen aufgeholt. "Warum soll das Europa und Deutschland nicht auch gelingen?", sagte er. Man verfüge in Europa zum anderen über wichtige Fertigkeiten, habe Datenschätze und arbeite an einer Souveränität der Infrastruktur.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Digitalminister Karsten Wildberger hat mit Blick auf die nötige Aufholjagd bei Künstlicher Intelligenz vor falschen Zielen gewarnt. "Es geht nicht immer nur darum, die Nummer eins zu sein", sagte Wildberger am Dienstag am Rande der Kabinettsklausur in Neuhardenberg. Deutschland sei die drittgrößte Volkswirtschaft, "und ich würde mal sagen, das Ziel, Nummer drei, Nummer vier zu sein in der Welt, ist auch mal ein gutes Zwischenziel", fügte er hinzu. Zwar seien Amerikaner und Chinesen beim Thema KI tatsächlich enteilt. Aber zum einen habe auch China mit weniger Ressourcen aufgeholt. "Warum soll das Europa und Deutschland nicht auch gelingen?", sagte er. Man verfüge in Europa zum anderen über wichtige Fertigkeiten, habe Datenschätze und arbeite an einer Souveränität der Infrastruktur. Wildberger warnte davor, sich mit einem unerreichbaren Ziel eine komfortable Entschuldigung zu schaffen, es bei der Aufholjagd erst gar nicht zu versuchen. Aber gerade beim industriellen Einsatz der KI sei Deutschland sehr stark. Man arbeite zudem mit Partnern in Kanada und Frankreich zusammen. "Wenn wir hier kraftvoll zusammenarbeiten, dann kann uns das auch gelingen", sagte der CDU-Politiker. Zuvor hatten bei der Klausurtagung nach Teilnehmerangaben die Unternehmenschefs von Siemens und Cohere, Roland Busch und Aidan Gomez, auf eine KI-Aufholjagd gerade bei der industriellen Nutzung gepocht.

item.title: Hubertz: Lege im Herbst Konzept für staatliche Wohnungsbaugesellschaft vor
item.description: Bauministerin Verena Hubertz hat angekündigt, im Herbst ein Konzept für die im Koalitionsausschuss beschlossene neue staatliche Wohnungsbaugesellschaft vorzulegen. Finanzminister Lars Klingbeil und sie hätten die Gründung einer solchen Gesellschaft vorgeschlagen, "die eben mal das große Rad dreht", sagte die SPD-Politikerin am Dienstag am Rande der Kabinettsklausur in Neuhardenberg. Dabei gehe es nicht um eine neue Behörde oder eine neue Baufirma, sondern darum, beide Welten zusammenzubringen. Es sollten "im großen Stil Aufträge vergeben (werden), die wir dann auch im seriellen Wohnungsbau mit Vorfahrt ausführen", sagte sie. "Dazu wollen wir im Herbst ein Konzept vorlegen und dann auch schnell in die Umsetzung kommen."
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bauministerin Verena Hubertz hat angekündigt, im Herbst ein Konzept für die im Koalitionsausschuss beschlossene neue staatliche Wohnungsbaugesellschaft vorzulegen. Finanzminister Lars Klingbeil und sie hätten die Gründung einer solchen Gesellschaft vorgeschlagen, "die eben mal das große Rad dreht", sagte die SPD-Politikerin am Dienstag am Rande der Kabinettsklausur in Neuhardenberg. Dabei gehe es nicht um eine neue Behörde oder eine neue Baufirma, sondern darum, beide Welten zusammenzubringen. Es sollten "im großen Stil Aufträge vergeben (werden), die wir dann auch im seriellen Wohnungsbau mit Vorfahrt ausführen", sagte sie. "Dazu wollen wir im Herbst ein Konzept vorlegen und dann auch schnell in die Umsetzung kommen." Um den immer noch schwachen Wohnungsbau in Deutschland anzukurbeln, müsse man einerseits Vorschriften und Normen abbauen, zum anderen aber skalieren. Wie etwa in der Automobilindustrie brauche man eine sogenannte serielle Produktion. "Wir können (dann) bauen bei Wind und Wetter, bei Hitze und Regen und Schnee", nannte Hubertz als Vorteil. "Deswegen ist es mein Ziel, dass die größten Fabriken im Land irgendwann auch mal für den Wohnungsbau da sind und nicht nur für andere Gewerke." Zudem müsse man länderübergreifend zusammenarbeiten, um dies auch rechtlich zu ermöglichen.

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, afirmou nesta terça-feira que todas as minas nas águas internacionais do Estreito de Ormuz foram removidas ou detonadas, e que o Irã havia sido notificado de que qualquer navio ou embarcação que colocar novas minas será destruído.

item.title: Rendimiento de bonos EEUU baja en medio de caída del crudo y debate sobre recompras del Tesoro
item.description: El rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro a más largo plazo caía el martes al tocar los precios del crudo un mínimo de una semana, mientras los operadores siguen sopesando las implicaciones de la decisión del secretario del Tesoro, Scott Bessent, de ampliar las recompras de bonos.
item.dc:creator: Karen Brettell
item.content:encoded: El rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro a más largo plazo caía el martes al tocar los precios del crudo un mínimo de una semana, mientras los operadores siguen sopesando las implicaciones de la decisión del secretario del Tesoro, Scott Bessent, de ampliar las recompras de bonos. * Los precios del petróleo caían más de 3%, ya que los operadores restaban importancia a la última campaña de sanciones de Estados Unidos contra Irán, al considerar que la presión económica supone un riesgo menor para el suministro petrolero que lo que supondría una escalada militar. * "Sigue habiendo una retórica muy acalorada y una escalada, pero el petróleo sigue cotizando en un rango estrecho teniendo en cuenta todo lo que ha ocurrido en los últimos meses", afirmó Will Compernolle, de FHN Financial. * Irán se comprometió a combatir las sanciones ampliadas de Estados Unidos destinadas a aislar su economía, expresando su confianza en que sus principales socios comerciales se resistirán a la campaña de presión, al tiempo que añadió que Washington sigue deseoso de reanudar las negociaciones. * Mientras, los operadores continúan debatiendo el plan del Tesoro de más que duplicar el volumen de sus recompras después de que Bessent afirmara que el reciente aumento de los rendimientos a largo plazo había ido demasiado lejos. * El retornos de los bonos a dos años , que suele evolucionar en paralelo a las expectativas sobre las tasas de interés de la Reserva Federal, caía 3,22 puntos básicos, al 4,204%, y el de las notas referenciales a 10 años <US10YT=RR> restaba 4,16 puntos básicos, al 4,662%. * La curva de rendimiento entre los papeles a dos y 10 años se aplanaba hasta situarse en 45 puntos básicos. * El Tesoro subastará más tarde en el día 69.000 millones de dólares en bonos a dos años, la primera de las subastas de deuda a corto y medio plazo por valor de 183.000 millones de dólares que se celebrarán esta semana.

item.title: トランプ氏、ホルムズ海峡の機雷「全て除去」 新たに設置なら破壊と警告
item.description: ［２５日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２５日　ロイター］ - トランプ米大統領は２５日、交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）「トゥルース・ソーシャル」への投稿で、ホルムズ海峡の国際水域に設置されていた全ての機雷が除去もしくは爆破されたとの報告を受けたと明らかにした。さらに、イランに対し、新たな機雷を設置する船舶は全て破壊すると通告したと述べた。

トランプ氏は投稿で、原油輸送の要衝であるホルムズ海峡について、米国は宇宙軍を通じて「隅々まで」監視していると強調。「機雷敷設に関しては、ゼロトレランス（不寛容）の方針が完全に施行されている」と述べた。

米国とイランは数週間にわたって互いの軍事施設への空爆を行っていないものの、ホルムズ海峡では船舶への攻撃が続いている。船舶追跡データ企業ボルテクサの暫定データによると、２４日にホルムズ海峡を通過した原油量は日量５００万バレルと、戦争前の約２０００万バレルの水準から大きく落ち込んでいる。

item.title: Las ventas de viviendas unifamiliares nuevas en EEUU caen en julio
item.description: Las ventas de viviendas unifamiliares nuevas en Estados Unidos se desplomaron en julio, ya que las elevadas tasas hipotecarias y los precios lastraron el mercado y siguieron disuadiendo a los posibles compradores.
item.dc:creator: Dan Burns
item.content:encoded: Las ventas de viviendas unifamiliares nuevas en Estados Unidos se desplomaron en julio, ya que las elevadas tasas hipotecarias y los precios lastraron el mercado y siguieron disuadiendo a los posibles compradores. Las ventas de viviendas nuevas cayeron un 10,5%, a una tasa anualizada destacionalizada de 607.000 unidades el mes pasado, frente al ritmo revisado al alza de junio, según informó el martes la Oficina del Censo del Departamento de Comercio. Las ventas de viviendas nuevas, que se contabilizan al formalizarse el contrato, representan una pequeña parte de las ventas inmobiliarias en Estados Unidos y suelen ser volátiles de un mes a otro. En junio cayeron un 6,3% en términos interanuales. Los economistas encuestados por Reuters habían estimado 620.000 unidades. El precio medio de las viviendas nuevas, de 393.800 dólares en julio, fue un 0,9% inferior al del año anterior. Los elevados costos de financiación son un factor clave que mantiene al mercado inmobiliario en una profunda crisis. La tasa de interés media de una hipoteca a 30 años con tasa fija —el tipo de préstamo hipotecario más popular en Estados Unidos— se sitúa cerca de un máximo de más de un año, con pocas perspectivas de un respiro inmediato, debido al temor a la inflación entre las autoridades de la Reserva Federal y en los mercados de bonos. La Asociación de Banqueros Hipotecarios señaló la semana pasada que la tasa contractual de las hipotecas a 30 años se mantuvo en el 6,77% en la semana que finalizó el 14 de agosto, apenas por debajo de su máximo reciente del 6,81% registrado a fines de julio. Las tasas hipotecarias han subido ya cerca de 0,6 puntos porcentuales desde que Estados Unidos e Israel lanzaron ataques contra Irán a fines de febrero, provocando un aumento de los precios mundiales del petróleo y contribuyendo a avivar la inflación en general. Los precios, según el indicador utilizado por la Fed para su objetivo de inflación del 2%, han estado subiendo a un ritmo casi el doble de ese, aunque los datos que se publicarán el miércoles podrían mostrar que se moderaron por segundo mes consecutivo en julio.

item.title: Deux décès dus à la rougeole en Pennsylvanie, une première en 35 ans
item.description: Deux habitants de Pennsylvanie sont décédés des suites de la rougeole, ont annoncé mardi les autorités sanitaires, une première dans l'Etat depuis 35 ans.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Deux habitants de Pennsylvanie sont décédés des suites de la rougeole, ont annoncé mardi les autorités sanitaires, une première dans l'Etat depuis 35 ans. Depuis le début de l'année 2026, 393 cas de la maladie ont été signalés dans 28 comtés. Les deux personnes étaient des habitants non-vaccinés du comté de Lancaster, selon le ministère de la Santé de Pennsylvanie, qui n'a pas communiqué davantage de détails, invoquant des raisons de confidentialité. "La rougeole ayant été pratiquement éradiquée dans l'État depuis plus de trois décennies, la population ne connaît pas bien cette maladie et n'en mesure pas pleinement la gravité potentielle”, a déclaré la secrétaire à la Santé, Debra Bogen. La rougeole a connu une forte recrudescence aux États-Unis cette année, les Centres pour le contrôle et la prévention des maladies (CDC) ayant recensé 2.777 cas confirmés à l'échelle nationale au 20 août. Les chiffres de 2026 représentent le nombre le plus élevé de cas enregistrés aux États-Unis en une seule année depuis la grande résurgence de cette maladie, hautement contagieuse, survenue entre 1989 et 1991, qui avait alors entraîné plus de 55.000 infections et 123 décès. Le ministère américain de la Santé et des Services sociaux n'ont pas immédiatement répondu à une demande de commentaire de Reuters.

item.title: Confiança do consumidor nos EUA cai em agosto, diz Conference Board
item.description: A confiança do consumidor nos Estados Unidos caiu em agosto para o nível mais baixo em sete meses uma vez que as perspectivas das famílias em relação ao mercado de trabalho e à inflação se deterioraram, segundo uma pesquisa divulgada nesta terça-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A confiança do consumidor nos Estados Unidos caiu em agosto para o nível mais baixo em sete meses uma vez que as perspectivas das famílias em relação ao mercado de trabalho e à inflação se deterioraram, segundo uma pesquisa divulgada nesta terça-feira. O Conference Board informou que seu índice de confiança do consumidor caiu para 89,4 neste mês — o menor nível desde janeiro —, ante 90,2 em julho em dado revisado para baixo. Economistas consultados pela Reuters previam que o índice ficaria em 90,2, contra os 90,8 de julho divulgado inicialmente. A queda foi liderada por uma perda de 7,8% no índice de expectativas, compensando a primeira melhora na percepção das famílias sobre a situação atual em quatro meses. “Os consumidores estavam mais pessimistas em relação às condições dos negócios e ao mercado de trabalho nos próximos seis meses”, afirmou Dana Peterson, economista-chefe do Conference Board. Os consumidores previram que a inflação vai acelerar nos próximos 12 meses, passando de 5,6% em julho para 5,8%. (Reportagem de Dan Burns)

item.title: 米国株は上昇、エヌビディア8日ぶり反発－原油安で米債利回り低下
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 25日午前の米株式相場は上昇している。原油価格の下落を受け、米国債利回りが低下した。市場関係者は26日のエヌビディア決算で、AIの先行きに対する強気な見方が維持されるかどうかを見極めようとしている。

エヌビディア株は8営業日ぶりに上昇。フィラデルフィア半導体株指数は一時2.5%上昇した。

米紙ニューヨーク・タイムズ（NYT）は、米国がイラン戦争開始後に中東の大使館から退避させていた外交官らを現地に戻す準備を進めていると報じた。戦争が激化するとの懸念が和らぎ、市場心理の改善に寄与している。

北海ブレント原油先物は1バレル＝90ドルを割り込んだ。NYTの報道に加え、イラン戦争の仲介国が、停戦に向けた取り組みを継続していると述べたことも影響した。

外国為替市場では、米国債利回り低下を受けてドル指数が下げている。ただ、円は対ドルで小幅安。米東部時間午前10時25分現在は、ニューヨーク前日比で0.1%安の1ドル＝159円28銭で取引されている。
